page: Microsoft Azure L2s_v4 is a storage-capable virtual machine belonging to the Lsv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. This instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, yielding 2 threads per core. The processor includes a cache configuration of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 260 MB L3 cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions).

The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 480 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not feature any GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core performance is relatively robust, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2138.0 and average stress-ng single-core CPU performance. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are more limited; the stress-ng multi-core performance is rated as poor, and large-block memory read and write bandwidths are measured at 20.23 GB/sec and 14.38 GB/sec respectively. Redis SET operations reach 2.85 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is recorded at 4.16 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L2s_v4 offers a high resource density of memory and local storage relative to its low vCPU count, making it a viable entry-level option for workloads requiring local data persistence without heavy multi-threaded compute demands. It is suited for lightweight database operations, basic web serving, single-threaded data processing, and small-scale caching workloads.
